mainTopic: The order of the morning עבודה in the היכל: why the inner מזבח comes before the מנורה, what רבא learns about תפילין from this, and the פסוק source for when the הטבת הנרות happens relative to דם התמיד.
overview: This amud continues אביי's list of the order of the morning עבודה. First the גמרא finishes ריש לקיש's reason why the inner מזבח is cleaned before the מנורה: when the כהן enters the היכל, the מזבח is the first thing he reaches, and you may not pass over a מצוה. A ברייתא about where the vessels stood proves this, and רבא applies the same rule to put on the arm תפילין before the head תפילין. Next, אביי explains why five lamps are cleaned before דם התמיד and two lamps after it. He uses the extra words 'בבקר בבקר' from the logs of wood and counts how many times 'בבקר' applies to each service. When the count is a tie, 'מכפר עדיף' decides. רב פפא suggests a different placement, and אביי answers that the lamps must be split by a service in between. That answer works according to רבי יוחנן but not according to ריש לקיש. רבינא asks whether those words are really extra, and רב אשי shows they are, because 'עליה' already teaches the order of the wood piles. The גמרא then explains why the first round is five lamps, and lists the next links: two lamps before the קטורת, the קטורת before the אברים, and the אברים before the מנחה. The source for that last link continues on the next amud.

steps.title: When entering the Sanctuary, the altar is reached first
steps.stepSummary: This explains why דישון מזבח הפנימי comes before הטבת חמש נרות. When the כהן walks into the היכל, the מזבח is the first vessel he reaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he enters the היכל, it is the מזבח that he reaches first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing ריש לקיש's explanation on the previous amud. It explains why the inner altar is cleaned before the lamps: the altar is the first thing the כהן reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's rule is אין מעבירין על המצוות, which means you may not walk past one מצוה to do another. Since the מזבח stands closer to the entrance than the מנורה, the כהן must take care of it first. This line tells us the physical fact that makes the rule apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary, the inner hall of the בית המקדש
Altar (here, the inner golden altar for incense)

steps.confusionAlert: This line continues an argument that began on the previous amud. 'He reaches the altar first' is the proof for ריש לקיש's rule of אין מעבירין על המצוות. It is not a new topic.

phrases.english: And when he enters the Sanctuary —
it is the altar that he encounters first.
phrases.notes: So he must take care of the altar before the candelabrum, because one may not pass over a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues ריש לקיש's reasoning on the previous amud (אין מעבירין על המצוות).

steps.title: A ברייתא describing where the vessels stood in the Sanctuary
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes the layout of the היכל. The שלחן was in the north and the מנורה in the south, each two and a half אמות from the wall. The מזבח was in the middle, pulled slightly outward.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: The שלחן stood in the north, two and a half אמות away from the wall. The מנורה stood in the south, two and a half אמות away from the wall. The מזבח was centered in the middle and pulled a little outward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that the מזבח really is the first vessel you reach when you enter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The entrance of the היכל is on the east side. Because the מזבח is placed a bit 'outward' (toward the entrance) compared to the שלחן and the מנורה, a כהן walking in reaches it before them. This supports the claim made in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: As it was taught: The table was in the north,

phrases.aramaic: מָשׁוּךְ מִן הַכּוֹתֶל שְׁתֵּי אַמּוֹת וּמֶחֱצָה,
phrases.english: pulled away from the wall two and a half cubits,
and the candelabrum was in the south,

phrases.aramaic: מְשׁוּכָה מִן הַכּוֹתֶל שְׁתֵּי אַמּוֹת וּמֶחֱצָה.
phrases.english: pulled away from the wall two and a half cubits.
The altar was centered, standing in the middle,
and pulled a bit toward the outside.
phrases.notes: That is, toward the entrance, so it is reached first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the textual support for step 1's claim that the מזבח is reached first.
steps.raayaObject: That the מזבח is the first vessel reached upon entering the היכל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing where the שלחן, מנורה, and מזבח stood.

steps.title: Why not line the altar up with the table and candelabrum?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the מזבח was pulled outward. Why not place it in a straight line between the שלחן and the מנורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And let us stand the מזבח in line with them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a side question about the ברייתא's layout. It wants to know why the מזבח is not in the same row as the other two vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If all three vessels stood in one straight line, the arrangement would seem neater. So the גמרא wants a reason for moving the מזבח forward.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us stand it (place it)
Alongside them, in line with them

phrases.english: And let us stand it alongside them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail of the ברייתא brought in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the מזבח is pulled outward instead of standing in line with the שלחן and מנורה.

steps.title: The table and candelabrum must face each other
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the מנורה stands 'opposite the שלחן'. So nothing may block the view between them, and the מזבח must be moved forward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is written, 'And the מנורה opposite the שלחן,' we need them to be able to see each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 3 using a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'נכח' (opposite) teaches that the שלחן and the מנורה must face each other directly. If the מזבח stood in the same line, it would stand between them and block them. So it is moved slightly outward, and that is exactly why it is reached first.

phrases.english: Since it is written:
"And the candelabrum opposite the table" (Exodus 26:35),
we require that they see each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פסוק requires the מנורה and שלחן to face each other with nothing in between, so the מזבח is moved forward.

steps.title: רבא: do not skip the arm תפילין to reach the head תפילין
steps.stepSummary: From ריש לקיש's rule, רבא learns that you may not pass over the תפילין של יד in order to put on the תפילין של ראש first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We can learn from ריש לקיש that it is forbidden to pass over the arm תפילין for the head תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes ריש לקיש's rule from the עבודה and applies it to a new, everyday case: putting on תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you take out your תפילין, you reach the arm תפילין first, just as the כהן reaches the מזבח first. Since אין מעבירין על המצוות, you may not skip the arm תפילין to put on the head one first.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, we may conclude

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה: the arm תפילין is put on before the head תפילין. The source is the principle of אין מעבירין על המצוות.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Conclude from Reish Lakish's statement
that passing over the arm phylacteries for the head phylacteries is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies ריש לקיש's principle from step 1 to תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not skip the arm תפילין to put on the head תפילין first.

steps.title: The practical order: arm first, then head
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a person should actually do. The answer: he goes from the arm תפילין to the head תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he act? From the arm to the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's teaching by stating the practical order for putting on תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns רבא's prohibition into a positive instruction: first the arm תפילין, then the head תפילין. It closes this side discussion.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's rule of אין מעבירין על המצוות explains two things. The inner מזבח comes before the מנורה, because it is reached first. The arm תפילין comes before the head תפילין, for the same reason.

phrases.english: How does he act?
From the arm phylacteries to the head phylacteries.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical result of step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One puts on the arm תפילין first and then the head תפילין.

steps.title: Five lamps before the תמיד's blood, and two lamps after
steps.stepSummary: אביי's order continues. The הטבת חמש נרות comes before דם התמיד, and דם התמיד comes before the הטבת שתי נרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the cleaning of five lamps comes before the blood of the תמיד, and the blood of the תמיד comes before the cleaning of two lamps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to אביי's list of the order of the morning עבודה and states the next link in the chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cleaning of the מנורה's seven lamps is split into two parts, with the תמיד's blood in between. First five lamps are cleaned, then the blood is offered, then the last two lamps are cleaned. The גמרא will now ask for the source of this split.

keyTerms.meaning: Cleaning and preparing the lamps of the מנורה
The blood of the daily morning offering

steps.confusionAlert: The seven lamps are not cleaned all at once. They are split 5 and 2, and the תמיד's blood comes in between.

phrases.english: And the removal of ashes from five lamps
precedes the blood of the daily offering,
and the blood of the daily offering precedes
the removal of ashes from two lamps.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲטָבַת חָמֵשׁ נֵרוֹת קוֹדֵם לְדַם הַתָּמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תפילין side point and returns to אביי's list of the עבודה order.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order is: five lamps, then the תמיד's blood, then the remaining two lamps.

steps.title: What is the reason for this order?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the order in step 7.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the lamps and the blood are arranged in this order. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא is looking for a source in the פסוקים, not just a logical reason. It wants to know which words teach this exact order.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for putting דם התמיד between the five lamps and the two lamps.

steps.title: אביי: the extra 'in the morning' words are moved here
steps.stepSummary: The words 'בבקר בבקר' written about the שני גזירי עצים are not needed there. So they are applied here: one to the five lamps and one to the תמיד's blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: That 'בבקר בבקר' written about the two logs is not needed there, so throw it here. Throw one to the five lamps, so they come before the blood of the תמיד. Throw one to the blood of the תמיד, so it comes before the two lamps.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from step 8. He takes extra words from another פסוק and uses them to set up the order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The time of the שני גזירי עצים is already known from another source, so the words 'בבקר בבקר' are extra there. When words are extra in their own place, we apply them elsewhere to teach something new. One 'בבקר' gives the five lamps an advantage over the blood, and the other gives the blood an advantage over the two lamps.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In the morning, in the morning,' a phrase that shows priority in the morning order
Logs of wood placed on the outer מזבח

phrases.english: Abaye said:
That phrase "in the morning, in the morning"
of the two logs, which is not needed there,
throw it to here.
Throw one to the removal of ashes from five lamps —
so that it will precede the blood of the daily offering;
and throw one to the blood of the daily offering —
so that it will precede the removal of ashes from two lamps.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָהוּא ״בַּבֹּקֶר בַּבֹּקֶר״ דִּשְׁנֵי גְּזִירֵי עֵצִים דְּלָא צְרִיכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'בבקר בבקר' of the logs is applied here: one to the five lamps and one to the תמיד's blood, which creates the order.

steps.title: Counting the 'mornings': three versus two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the five lamps come before the blood: the lamps now have three mentions of 'בבקר', and the blood has only two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Throw one to the five lamps so they come before the blood of the תמיד, because here there are three and here there are two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the first half of אביי's answer to explain how it works: we count how many times 'בבקר' applies to each service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lamps already have two 'בבקר' written in their own פסוק, and with the extra one they have three. The תמיד's blood has one written in its own פסוק, and with the extra one it has two. The service with more 'mornings' comes first, so the five lamps come before the blood.
steps.confusionAlert: The repetition here is not a mistake. The גמרא repeats the line in order to show the counting: the service with more 'בבקר' mentions comes first.
steps.whatToRemember: The order is based on counting the words 'בבקר'. Lamps: 2 + 1 extra = 3. Blood of the תמיד: 1 + 1 extra = 2. Three beats two, so the five lamps come first.

phrases.english: Throw one to the removal of ashes from five lamps,
so that it will precede the blood of the daily offering —
for here there are three and here there are two.
phrases.notes: Lamps: two written plus one extra. Blood: one written plus one extra.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד שִׁדְיֵיהּ לַהֲטָבַת חָמֵשׁ נֵרוֹת, דְּלִיקְדְּמֵיהּ לְדַם הַתָּמִיד — דְּהָכָא תְּלָתָא וְהָכָא תְּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats and explains the first half of אביי's answer in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lamps have three mentions of 'בבקר' and the blood has two, so the lamps come first.

steps.title: Why the blood comes before the last two lamps
steps.stepSummary: The second extra 'בבקר' goes to דם התמיד, so the blood comes before the הטבת שתי נרות. Each side then has two mentions, so the tie is broken by the rule that an atoning act comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other extra 'בבקר' is given to the blood of the תמיד, so that it comes before cleaning the two lamps. Each side has two mentions, but the act that brings atonement wins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining אביי's order. It shows why the blood of the תמיד comes before the cleaning of the last two lamps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the extra 'בבקר' is added, the blood has two mentions and the two lamps also have two mentions, so counting does not decide. The tie-breaker is a different rule: an act that brings כפרה (the blood) comes before one that does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Throw it, meaning: apply the extra word to a different place
Cleaning and preparing the last two lamps of the מנורה
An act that brings atonement takes priority

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the count of 'בבקר' decides this case. Here the count is equal, two against two, and the separate rule of 'מכפר עדיף' breaks the tie.

phrases.english: And one, throw it to the blood of the daily offering
phrases.notes: The second extra 'בבקר' from the שני גזירי עצים

phrases.english: so that it comes before the cleaning of the two lamps

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּהָכָא תְּרֵי וְהָכָא תְּרֵי
phrases.english: Even though here there are two and here there are two
the one that atones takes precedence

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation begun in step 10. Step 10 justified five lamps before the blood, and this step justifies the blood before the two lamps.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does דם התמיד come before the הטבת שתי נרות?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One extra 'בבקר' goes to the blood, making it two against two. The tie is broken because an atoning act takes precedence.

steps.title: רב פפא suggests a different way to use the extra words
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי why not use the extra 'בבקר' words differently. One could go to דישון מזבח הפנימי, putting it before the blood, three against two. The other could go to the blood, putting it before the five lamps, two against two, with the atoning act winning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Why not say it differently? Give one extra 'בבקר' to cleaning the inner altar, so it comes before the blood, since that would be three against two. Give the other to the blood, so it comes before the five lamps. Even though each side has two, the atoning act wins!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges אביי by showing the same two extra words could be placed differently. That would produce a different order of services.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא uses אביי's own tools: counting mentions of 'בבקר' and the rule of 'מכפר עדיף'. In his version, the blood moves ahead of all seven lamps instead of sitting between the five and the two. The point is that אביי's placement seems arbitrary.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead (proposes an alternative reading)
Clearing the ashes from the inner (golden) altar
The אמורא who challenges אביי here

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye
But say instead
throw one to the clearing of ashes of the inner altar
so that it comes before the blood of the daily offering
since here there are three and here there are two
And throw one to the blood of the daily offering
so that it comes before the cleaning of the five lamps

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּהָכָא תְּרֵי וְהָכָא תְּרֵי
phrases.english: for even though here there are two and here there are two
the one that atones takes precedence!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי, וְאֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the derivation in steps 9–11 by proposing a different placement of the same extra words.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's placement of the two extra 'בבקר' words (five lamps, then blood, then two lamps)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same counting method and the 'מכפר עדיף' rule could just as easily put the blood before all the lamps. So אביי's order is not forced by the פסוקים.

steps.title: אביי: Then what would separate the lamps?
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that in רב פפא's order nothing comes between the five lamps and the two lamps. Yet the lamp-cleaning must be split by something in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, with what would you separate them (the five lamps from the two lamps)?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his order with a short counter-question. The lamp-cleaning is supposed to be split, and רב פפא's order leaves no service in the middle to split it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אביי's order, דם התמיד sits between the five lamps and the two lamps and acts as the divider. In רב פפא's order, the blood moves earlier, so the five and the two would be done back-to-back. That defeats the required split.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if we accept your suggestion)

phrases.english: If so
to separate them, with what would you separate them?
phrases.notes: Separating the five lamps from the two lamps

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן אַפְסוֹקֵי בְּמַאי מַפְסְקַתְּ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a structural flaw in the alternative: it fails to separate the two stages of lamp-cleaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא thought the extra words could be placed in any order that fits the counting rules.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blood must stay between the five and the two lamps, because something has to divide them.

steps.title: According to ריש לקיש, רב פפא's order works fine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that אביי's answer would not work for ריש לקיש. For him, the lamps are split only to make the courtyard busy, and no separating service is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to ריש לקיש, who said: Why do they clean lamps and then come back and clean more lamps? To create activity throughout the whole courtyard. According to him, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It admits that according to ריש לקיש, רב פפא's order would cause no problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש says the lamp-cleaning is split only to make the courtyard bustle with people. That goal does not require any other service in the middle. So for him, 'with what will you separate?' is not a real problem, and רב פפא's order could stand.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (according to one opinion)
The אמורא whose reason for splitting the lamps is creating activity

phrases.english: This works well according to Reish Lakish, who said
Why do they clean lamps and then return and clean again?
in order to stir up activity in the entire courtyard
it is fine

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits אביי's answer from step 13 by showing it does not hold according to ריש לקיש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to ריש לקיש, the lamps are split only to create activity, so no service must stand in between.

steps.title: According to רבי יוחנן, a real split is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads 'בבקר בבקר' as requiring the lamp-cleaning to be divided into 'two mornings'. That needs a real break between the five and the two lamps, so רב פפא's order cannot work and אביי's order stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי יוחנן, who said that 'בבקר בבקר' means divide it into two mornings, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that אביי's answer is solid according to רבי יוחנן. It ends with a question that has no answer, which means רב פפא's order fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן learns from the doubled 'בבקר בבקר' that the lamp-cleaning must happen in two separate stages. That requires a service in between. Only אביי's order provides that divider, with דם התמיד in the middle. So 'מאי איכא למימר' means there is nothing to say for רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who requires splitting the lamp-cleaning into two mornings
What can be said? (there is no answer)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's order is: five lamps, then the blood of the תמיד, then two lamps. The blood stands in the middle because, per רבי יוחנן, the lamp-cleaning must be split by a real service. רב פפא's alternative would only work for ריש לקיש.
steps.confusionAlert: 'מאי איכא למימר' here is not a real open question. It is rhetorical and means רב פפא's suggestion cannot work for רבי יוחנן, so אביי is right.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the order of the Temple service depends on the reason behind a rule. The two אמוראים give different reasons for splitting the lamps, and each reason leads to a different possible order.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yochanan, who said
'In the morning, in the morning'
divide it into two mornings
what can be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'הניחא... אלא' structure begun in step 14, showing אביי's answer holds according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Grounds אביי's rebuttal in רבי יוחנן's requirement of a real division between the two stages of lamp-cleaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Per ריש לקיש, רב פפא's order would be acceptable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Per רבי יוחנן, a service must separate the five lamps from the two, so the blood must be in between, as אביי said.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי's order stands according to רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Is the doubled 'in the morning' about the wood really extra?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב אשי: the 'בבקר בבקר' written about the wood seems needed for its own teaching, that the logs come before the second pile for the קטורת. If so, it is not extra and cannot be used to set the order of other services.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: This 'in the morning, in the morning' written about the wood, is it really extra? It is needed for its own point, that the Torah is saying: let the logs come before the second pile, the one for the קטורת!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks a building block of אביי's order. אביי treated the doubled 'בבקר' about the wood as an extra word that could be used to place other services.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra word can only be used for something new if it is not already needed for its plain meaning. רבינא says the plain meaning is busy: the doubled word teaches that the two logs come before the second pile. If that is so, the word has no room left to teach anything else.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really extra (free to teach something new)?
The two logs of wood added each morning
The second pile of wood on the מזבח, from which coals are taken for the incense

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
This 'in the morning, in the morning' said about the logs,
is it really extra?
It is needed for its own point,
phrases.notes: So it would have no room to teach anything else.

phrases.english: for the Merciful One is saying:
Let them (the logs) come before the second pile, the one for incense!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to אביי's premise in step 9 (that the 'בבקר בבקר' of the logs is extra) and questions whether it really is extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the 'בבקר בבקר' written about the wood is extra and can be used to place other services.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A word that is needed for its own plain teaching cannot also be used for another teaching.

steps.title: The word 'on it' already shows the second pile came first
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the word 'עליה' (on it, and not on the other pile) already teaches that the second pile exists when the logs are added. So the order of logs and second pile is already known, and the doubled 'בבקר' stays extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't we already explain that 'on it' means on the big pile and not on the other pile? That shows the other pile is already there.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends אביי. The order between the logs and the second pile comes from another word, so the doubled 'בבקר' is still free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the כהן puts wood 'עליה', on it, which means on the big pile and not on the other one. You only need to say 'not on the other pile' if the other pile is already standing there. So the second pile comes before the logs, and the doubled 'בבקר' is not needed for this point.

keyTerms.meaning: We have already explained (set the meaning)
On it, and not on its companion (the other pile)
This implies that it already exists

steps.whatToRemember: The second pile comes before the two logs. We learn this from 'עליה', so the doubled 'בבקר' about the wood stays extra.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Didn't we already explain
'on it' and not on its companion pile,
which implies that the companion pile is already there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to another source that already teaches the point, so the word in question stays extra
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubled 'בבקר' is needed to put the logs before the second pile.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'עליה ולא על חברתה' shows the second pile already exists, so the doubled 'בבקר' is free for other uses.

steps.title: Why clean five lamps first and not two?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first round of lamp-cleaning covers five lamps and the second round covers two. Why not clean two first and then five?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is it that he cleans five lamps first? Let him clean two lamps first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new detail in the order. It asks why the lamp-cleaning is split as five, then two, and not two, then five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 13 and 15 already showed that the lamp-cleaning must be split into two parts. Now the question is only about which part is bigger and goes first.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why this way?
Cleaning and preparing the lamps of the מנורה

phrases.english: Why is it that he performs
the cleaning of five lamps first?
Let him clean two lamps first!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא דְּעָבֵיד הֲטָבַת חָמֵשׁ נֵרוֹת בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the split of the lamp-cleaning (Steps 13 and 15) and asks how the split is made.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the bigger group of lamps (five) is cleaned first.

steps.title: Once you start, do most of the lamps
steps.stepSummary: Since the כהן has already started the lamp-cleaning, he does most of the lamps, five out of seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he has started with them, he does the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that once a job has been started, you do most of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Five out of seven is a majority, so the first round covers most of the lamps. Doing only two at the start would be a weak beginning to a job that is already underway.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he has started with them

phrases.english: Since he has started with them,
he does the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Once started, he does the majority of the lamps, which is five.

steps.title: Then why not clean six?
steps.stepSummary: If the goal is to do as much as possible once you start, the כהן should clean six lamps first and leave only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him do six!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the last answer further. If you do most of the lamps once you start, why stop at five?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea of 'doing the majority' does not explain why the number is exactly five. Six is also a majority, and an even bigger one.

phrases.english: Then let him do six!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason 'once started, do the majority'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the goal is to do as much as possible, six would be even better than five.

steps.title: The second round needs at least two lamps
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'when he cleans the lamps', using the plural. The plural means at least two, so the second round must cover two lamps. That leaves five for the first round.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'When he cleans the lamps, he shall burn it (the incense),' and 'lamps' means no fewer than two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The lamp-cleaning that goes with the קטורת must cover at least two lamps, so the first round can be at most five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הנרות' is plural, and a plural means at least two. Since the later round needs two lamps, only five are left for the first round. That is the most the first round can include.

keyTerms.meaning: When he cleans the lamps, he shall burn it (the incense)

steps.whatToRemember: Five lamps come first because the second round must cover at least two lamps, since 'נרות' is plural. Five is the biggest majority that still leaves two.

phrases.english: The verse says:
'When he cleans the lamps, he shall burn it,'
and 'lamps' means no fewer than two.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: בְּהֵיטִיבוֹ אֶת הַנֵּרוֹת יַקְטִירֶנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק sets a minimum number for the second round
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He could clean six lamps first and leave only one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second round must be at least two lamps ('נרות' is plural), so the first round is five.

steps.title: The two lamps come before the incense
steps.stepSummary: אביי's order continues: cleaning the two lamps comes before the קטורת. The פסוק says 'when he cleans the lamps' first and only then 'he shall burn it'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And cleaning the two lamps comes before the incense, as the פסוק says 'when he cleans the lamps,' and only after that 'he shall burn it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to listing אביי's order. It explains the next link: the two lamps, then the קטורת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק used in Step 21 also gives the order. It mentions the cleaning first and the burning of the incense afterward, so the cleaning comes first in practice too.

phrases.english: And cleaning the two lamps comes before the incense,
for the verse says: 'When he cleans the lamps,'
and afterward 'he shall burn it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to אביי's chain of sources after the side question about five and two lamps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cleaning the two lamps comes before the קטורת, following the order of the words in the פסוק.

steps.title: The incense comes before the limbs
steps.stepSummary: The קטורת comes before burning the אברים of the תמיד. A ברייתא teaches that a service written with 'בבקר בבקר' comes before a service written with only one 'בקר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the incense comes before the limbs, as a ברייתא teaches: Let the thing about which it says 'in the morning, in the morning' come before the thing about which it says only one 'morning'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the next link in אביי's order: קטורת, then the אברים. It brings a ברייתא as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קטורת is written with a doubled 'בבקר בבקר', while the תמיד lamb is written with only one 'בבקר'. The ברייתא's rule is that the service with the doubled word comes first. This is the same kind of 'count the בבקר words' reasoning that אביי used throughout.

keyTerms.meaning: The limbs of the תמיד offering, burned on the outer מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: Order so far: two lamps, then קטורת, then אברים. Wherever the Torah writes 'בבקר' twice, that service comes before one with only one 'בבקר'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא confirms the method used in the whole סוגיא: the number of times 'בבקר' appears decides which service comes first.

phrases.english: And the incense comes before the limbs,
as it was taught in a baraita:
Let the thing about which 'in the morning, in the morning' is said come first,
before the thing about which is said
only a single 'morning.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's chain to the next service in the order.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קטורת (written with 'בבקר בבקר') comes before the אברים of the תמיד (written with only one 'בבקר').

steps.title: The limbs come before the meal-offering
steps.stepSummary: אביי's order continues: burning the אברים of the תמיד comes before the מנחה. The גמרא starts bringing a ברייתא as the source, which asks how we know that nothing may come before the morning תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the limbs come before the meal-offering. As a ברייתא teaches: From where do we know that nothing may come before the morning תמיד?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the next link in אביי's chain: the אברים are burned before the מנחה. It then begins quoting a ברייתא as proof. This is a setup line, and the ברייתא's answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 put the קטורת before the אברים. Now the אברים are placed before the מנחה. The ברייתא opens by asking for a source that the morning תמיד must be the very first offering on the מזבח. That rule is the basis for putting the תמיד's limbs ahead of the מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: The limbs (body parts) of the תמיד that are burned on the מזבח
The flour meal-offering that comes along with the תמיד
As a ברייתא teaches (introduces a teaching of the תנאים)
From where do we know? (asks for a source)

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'מניין' is not an attack on אביי. It is the ברייתא's own opening question, and the ברייתא will answer it from a פסוק. The answer is what supports אביי's order.

phrases.english: And the limbs come before the meal-offering,
phrases.notes: Short form: the limbs come first, then the meal-offering.

phrases.english: as it was taught in a baraita: From where do we know
phrases.notes: Introduces the source and its opening question.

phrases.english: that no item may come before
phrases.notes: Nothing may be placed on the מערכה first.

phrases.english: the daily morning offering?
phrases.notes: The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's chain of service order (קטורת before אברים, now אברים before מנחה) and begins bringing its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning the אברים of the תמיד comes before offering the מנחה, based on a ברייתא that says nothing may come before the morning תמיד.
